purpose: Modern Python 3 CLI entry point and console-script target for the ASCII movie player. It validates arguments with argparse, keeps safe local server defaults, and routes to either the threaded TCP server or stdout renderer.
invariants: Standalone mode defaults to 127.0.0.1:2323; public interface 0.0.0.0 and privileged port 23 must be explicit user choices.
The -f/--file argument is required and main rejects nonexistent files through argparse before opening sockets or playing output.
TelnetRequestHandler.filename must be set before ThreadedTCPServer begins serving so each connection can load the selected movie.
stdout mode decodes player buffers as iso-8859-15 to preserve the original terminal stream behavior.
runTcpServer and runStdOut remain aliases for compatibility with callers using the original script API.
gotchas: main() returns 130 on KeyboardInterrupt but argparse validation still raises SystemExit for usage errors.
run_tcp_server blocks in serve_forever() until interrupted.
The installed console script is defined in pyproject.toml, so packaging changes can affect CLI availability.

key_functions.name: build_parser
key_functions.summary: Constructs the argparse parser and documents standalone/stdout mode options.

key_functions.name: main
key_functions.summary: Parses argv, validates the movie file, routes to server or stdout mode, and maps KeyboardInterrupt to exit code 130.

key_functions.name: run_tcp_server
key_functions.summary: Sets the handler-wide movie filename, constructs ThreadedTCPServer, and blocks in serve_forever().

key_functions.name: run_stdout
key_functions.summary: Loads a Movie, overrides VT100Player.draw_frame to write decoded buffers to an output stream, then plays synchronously.
